mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 60-day high-rate period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns fail to outperform a 200-day rolling average during periods of similar labor strength (IC < 0.02).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above trend, unaccompanied by a proportional rise in industrial production (INDPRO), indicates robust consumer demand that drives equity price appreciation in the near term.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL exceeds its 6-month moving average by > 1.5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically significant relative to a 100-day baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in manufacturing activity (INDPRO) of more than 5% over two months suggests supply-side constraints, which can lead to elevated risk premia and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases for 2 consecutive months by > 5%
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly worse than during the prior 30-day expansion phase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%, it predicts a shift toward tighter policy, which reduces the discount rate applied to equities and results in negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite the policy signal (IC < -0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) followed by a sustained increase in labor force participation (PAYEMS) indicates a demographic or policy shift that boosts economic momentum and supports positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by > 0.3 percentage points while PAYEMS increases by > 1% over the next month
regime_hint: labor market expansion due to demographic changes
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform a 90-day historical average during similar labor expansion episodes (IC > 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous peak in consumer confidence (not directly observable here) and S&P 500 10-day returns suggests a self-reinforcing feedback loop where positive market sentiment drives further equity appreciation, producing positive 20-day forward returns when both signals align.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically significant when GDPC1 shows high volatility but no clear trend (IC > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: During a period of falling FEDFUNDS but stable industrial production (INDPRO), the lower discount rate applied to future cash flows from equities leads to positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns as the present value of expected profits increases.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decreases for 2 consecutive months while INDPRO remains flat
regime_hint: monetary policy normalization with stable supply
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from a baseline of stable policy and production (IC > 0.05).
